title: Team-scoped models must be on IDOR semgrep lists and a fail-closed EnvironmentScopedManager
answers: How to make a model environment scoped without leaking sibling environments' rows
Why does the model have all_teams and objects managers?
body: A new per-environment model must (1) use `objects = EnvironmentScopedManager()` (filters by literal team id, so sibling environments cannot read it) with `all_teams = models.Manager()` and `Meta.default_manager_name = "all_teams"` (products/tracing/backend/models.py:TracesRetentionRule), and (2) be added to BOTH class-name alternation lists in .semgrep/rules/security/idor-team-scoped-models.yaml. `.github/scripts/check-idor-model-coverage.py` checks this; skipping either fails CI or leaves an IDOR blind spot.
applies: New models with a team FK in PostHog products.
says: Data in one environment must not leak to sibling environments
New models for environment-specific data need security checks in CI
How to safely add retention or configuration models
Team scoping prevents users from seeing data outside their environment
Multiple database managers protect against accidental cross-environment contamination
search: New per-environment models with a team FK must implement fail-closed IDOR protection via two mandatory steps. (1) Set `objects = EnvironmentScopedManager()` (filters by literal team id, blocking sibling environment access), `all_teams = models.Manager()`, and `Meta.default_manager_name = "all_teams"`, as shown in products/tracing/backend/models.py:TracesRetentionRule. (2) Add the model class name to BOTH class-name alternation lists in .semgrep/rules/security/idor-team-scoped-models.yaml. The CI check .github/scripts/check-idor-model-coverage.py enforces both requirements; omitting either fails CI or leaves an IDOR vulnerability in unscan positions.
